correctness.rationale: Direct diagonalization of the 4-by-4 Hamiltonian gives the stated Gibbs X-state. Wootters' formula reduces positivity exactly to \(J\sinh(\eta/T)/\eta>e^{-J_z/T}\), \(\eta=\sqrt{J^2+b^2}\). Since \(x\cosh x-\sinh x>0\) for \(x>0\), \(\sinh x/x\) is strictly increasing, proving the one-threshold topology and the monotone \(J_z\)-dependence. Dominant hyperbolic terms give \(C\sim J/\eta\sim J/|b|\). A fresh independent matrix replay agreed with the closed formula to about \(5.4\times10^{-12}\) over a representative grid and produced \(|b|C/J=0.99875,0.99980,0.99995\) at \(|b|=20,50,100\).
risks: The theorem is only for the stated signs \(J>0\), \(J_z\ge0\); other sign regimes are outside scope.

value.rationale: Correcting a published qualitative phase-boundary interpretation is substantively useful: it changes 'entanglement dies above a finite inhomogeneity' into a one-sided activation law with a positive algebraic tail. The motivation is therefore strong even though the derivation is too directly implied by the prior exact formula to satisfy originality.
risks: The mathematical derivation is elementary once the published concurrence formula is in hand, which is why originality fails despite the physical usefulness.

final_claim: For the antiferromagnetic two-qubit XXZ Gibbs family with \(J>0\), \(J_z\ge0\), the concurrence positivity set has no finite upper inhomogeneity cutoff: it is either positive for all finite \(b\), positive for every nonzero \(b\) at the boundary, or activates once above a unique lower threshold; when that threshold exists it decreases with \(J_z\), and \(C(T,b)\sim J/|b|\).
limitations: No claim is made for ferromagnetic transverse coupling, negative \(J_z\), or monotonicity of concurrence magnitude at all parameters.
